clue.text: Warner embraces crazy nude, regular swinger

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: Sir Pelham Warner, the England cricket captain, was universally known as Plum

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the word nude are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A man called Warner hugs a mad naked swinger.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelham 'Plum' Warner was a famous English cricketer and administrator. 'Crazy' scrambles NUDE into ENDU, which 'embraces' puts inside PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's weighted bob swings to and fro at a steady, regular rate.

clue.text: Last words — of the elegy

parts.note: Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard closes with a section given its own heading: the closing verse is the inscription for a grave

explanation.definitionFit: Gray's famous Elegy ends with a short tomb inscription, the dead man's final words in stone.

clue.text: Shame, to take one off the birthday list?

definitions.meaning: shame as a noun means disgrace or loss of good name

definitions.text: to take one off the birthday list?
definitions.meaning: the Birthday Honours list is the twice-yearly British roll of royal awards; removing someone from it would un-award them

explanation.walkthrough: The Birthday Honours is the list of knighthoods and medals published on the British monarch's official birthday; the question mark flags the jokey reading DIS-HONOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace and loss of reputation; read in two parts, it is the reverse of conferring an award.

clue.text: Keep in touch with children's story about three-toed sloths

indicators.note: about means going around, so the fib wraps round the animals

parts.note: a story in the nursery sense is a fib, a childish word for an untruth
the ai is the three-toed sloth of South America, a crossword favourite; plural ais

explanation.surface: Someone stays in contact via a nursery tale about tree-hanging sloths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts AIS inside LIE, splitting it as LI...E. The ai is the three-toed sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a go-between, staying in contact and coordinating with another party.

clue.text: This name wasn't Ludwig's bright idea

definitions.text: This name wasn't Ludwig's bright idea

parts.words: This name wasn't Ludwig's bright idea
parts.note: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 14 got its popular title from the critic Rellstab after the composer's death, so Ludwig never thought of it

explanation.definitionFit: The critic Ludwig Rellstab likened the first movement to moonlight on Lake Lucerne; Beethoven only called it a fantasy-like sonata.

clue.text: Mother Adamson turns into a bedlamite

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: turns tells us the son's name is read the other way round

parts.note: Cain was a son of Adam in Genesis, so literally an Adam-son

explanation.surface: A mother named Adamson goes mad and becomes an asylum inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: Adamson looks like a surname (Joy Adamson of Born Free) but means 'son of Adam', CAIN; 'turns' reverses it to NIAC after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam was London's notorious madhouse, so a bedlamite is a lunatic.

clue.text: Scope for sentimentality with growth of atom warfare

parts.note: mush is soppy, sentimental stuff
scope in the sense of space or opportunity, as in room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A complaint that nuclear war leaves too much space for gushing sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Scope for sentimentality' as ROOM for MUSH, the sentiment coming first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear explosion sends up a cloud shaped like a fungus with a stalk and cap.

clue.text: Sort of rum 3-D element

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, signalling that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 3 in Roman numerals is III, followed by the letter D

explanation.surface: A peculiar three-dimensional element of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: '3-D' is taken as III (Roman three) plus D; with RUM, 'Sort of' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, dense metal of the platinum group in the periodic table.

clue.text: General view on Sunday opening in a counting of heads

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the count

parts.note: a census is an official head count of a population
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head count opening on a Sunday establishes what most people think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday opening' gives S; ON plus S goes 'in' CENSUS after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad agreement among a group, the opinion most people share.

clue.text: Disapproving word to saint taking a holiday

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust or reproach

explanation.surface: A saint being tutted at for going off on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival or feast day, a public celebration in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Glass Rock side, incomplete, gets one in Scottish town

indicators.note: in puts the preceding pieces inside the town's name

parts.note: Oban is a port town on the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: incomplete means the word side loses its last letter

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A side of rock, unfinished, is found in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' cuts SIDE to SID; add I, and that sits 'in' OBAN after OB. Oban is a west-coast Scottish port.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark volcanic glass that forms when lava cools too fast to crystallise.

clue.text: Musical merry-go-round

definitions.meaning: a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1945
a fairground ride of revolving horses

explanation.definitionFit: Both the 1945 Broadway show and a revolving fairground roundabout with wooden horses.

clue.text: Gunner Tree found plundering

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners
the pine is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: An artilleryman discovered looting beside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for pillage, seizing property by force.

clue.text: Photograph fire

definitions.meaning: to photograph or film a scene

explanation.definitionFit: Both taking pictures with a camera and discharging a gun at a target.

clue.text: Does it suit penitents to kick out the vicar?

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss from a job
the cloth is the clergy collectively, a vicar being one of them

explanation.surface: A question whether penitent worshippers would like to see the vicar dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' means the clergy, so a vicar stands for it; 'suit' is a pun on a suit of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sacking cloth worn as a sign of mourning or repentance, as in sackcloth and ashes.

clue.text: He doesn't know I'm on sugar metabolism

indicators.note: metabolism breaks down and rebuilds substances, so the letters are broken down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone admits ignorance while saying they are on a sugar diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metabolism' rearranges the nine letters of I'M ON SUGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant person, one lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Worker imprisoning chief is an anti-Government type

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the insect goes round the other pieces

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect
arch means chief, as in arch-enemy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A labourer locks up his boss, the act of a rebel against the state.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT splits as AN...T, 'imprisoning' ARCH and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects all state authority and wants it abolished.

clue.text: Christopher about to settle in a small way

indicators.note: about means around, so the surname surrounds the verb

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in the opening of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
to light, as a bird lights on a branch, is to land and settle

explanation.surface: A man called Christopher is about to calm down a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Sly is the tinker of Shakespeare's Taming of the Shrew prologue; 'about' wraps SLY round LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To a minor degree, only a little.

clue.text: To establish correspondence tell story about gold first

indicators.note: first says the about-and-gold pair comes before the storytelling verb

parts.note: c is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
or is the heraldic word for gold
to relate is to narrate or tell

explanation.surface: Instructions for writing letters: recount a tale, mentioning gold first.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) and OR (heraldic gold) are placed 'first', before RELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a mutual relation or connection between two things.

clue.text: One attending a Moscow stag party ?

definitions.text: One attending a Moscow stag party ?

parts.words: One attending a Moscow stag party
parts.note: a Russian communist is a Red, and a stag is a male deer, so a guest at a Muscovite stag do would be both

explanation.definitionFit: A large deer species; Red is the old nickname for a Soviet communist and a stag is the male.

clue.text: Reports of hair styles

definitions.meaning: loud explosive noises, as a gun reports
a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead, in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: Both loud explosive noises and fringes cut straight across the forehead, the American word for that cut.

clue.text: Rugged, knobbly ? Possible danger if about 50

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the numeral
possible here suggests a possible rearrangement of the word danger

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A warning that rough, knotty terrain could be risky at about fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotty and twisted, like an old tree trunk or arthritic hands.

clue.text: Description of the last Henry, bottom to top

definitions.meaning: the last English king of that name was the Eighth, so described as H plus a number
a measurement taken from base to summit

explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was the last King Henry; written as H EIGHT his title spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical measurement of something, from its base to its top.

clue.text: Giving up gardening work, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: seeding is sowing seeds in the garden

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their work in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrendering or yielding something, such as territory.

clue.text: It can be made to cover a suit

definitions.text: It can be made to cover a suit

parts.words: It can be made to cover a suit
parts.note: made to measure like a suit, a heavy outer garment worn on top of a suit in cold weather

explanation.definitionFit: A warm outer garment worn over other clothes, including a suit.

clue.text: A small musical work before the race, note

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
ere is a poetic word for before
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A short piece of music played ahead of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks part of the definition but gives OP; the TT is the Isle of Man's Tourist Trophy motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, light opera with spoken dialogue, a small-scale musical stage work.

clue.text: Horrifying, the bear sounds

indicators.note: sounds says we want a word pronounced like the bear's name

parts.note: the grizzly is the large North American brown bear

explanation.surface: The noises the bear makes are terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome, causing horror or disgust.

clue.text: Unorthodox opinion introduces X's successor

parts.note: here's is the phrase used to introduce someone, as in here's the next guest
Y follows X in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A dissenting view brings in someone's successor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Here's Y', introducing Y, the letter after X.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief contrary to accepted doctrine, especially in religion.

clue.text: 21 a banner-bearing youth hoped to gain

definitions.meaning: a cross-reference to the answer of 21 down, a vertical measurement

definitions.text: a banner-bearing youth hoped to gain
definitions.meaning: in Longfellow's poem Excelsior a youth carries a banner reading Excelsior (ever higher) up an Alpine pass

explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's youth climbs ever upward carrying his Excelsior banner, seeking to rise higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation above sea level, which the climber of Longfellow's poem kept striving to increase.
